newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cie des Signaux sees 1997 oper loss.
newsitem.headline: Cie des Signaux sees 1997 oper loss.

text.p: Compagnie des Signaux said on Wednesday it expected to show an operating loss of 50 million to 100 million francs this year but a positive operating margin from 1998.

The electrical signalling company said in a statement that chairman Yazid Sabeg told an analysts' meeting that the group's objective in the next three years was 15 percent sales growth and a seven percent operating margin.

The acquisition of three companies in the first half of 1997 -- Philips Communication d'Entreprise, CISI and Ritzenthaler -- will double Compagnie des Signaux's (CS) full-year sales to four billion francs, or over 3.4 billion for 1997 on a consolidated basis taking into account the acquisition dates, it said.

"Given the operating losses of the activities acquired, 1997 will be dedicated to restoring their profitability and placing them in a favourable position to benefit from expected strong growth in their markets from 1998," it said.
"CS should therefore show a consolidated operating loss of between 50 and 100 million francs in 1997 and recover a positive operating margin from 1998," it said.
Compagnie des Signaux said its cash position should be around 200 million francs at the end of the year.
